County of Los Angeles
Department of Public Social Services

GENERAL RELIEF PROGRAM
FACT SHEET

General Relief (GR) assists Los Angeles County residents who are not eligible for other
State or federal cash assistance programs. GR includes a monthly cash grant of $221 for
a single person, or $375 for a married couple, and access to supportive services. An
average GR case consists of one person, living alone, with no income or resources.

ELIGIBILITY REQUIREMENTS

To be eligible for GR, an individual must be a resident of Los Angeles County and be a
U.S. citizen or have a satisfactory immigration status. The GR eligibility requirements
are:

+ Monthly net income is lower than the maximum GR grant of $221 for one person or
$375 for a married couple.

+ Personal property has a combined value of $2,000 or less.

+ The property limit for an owned motor vehicle used as a residence is $11,500. Motor
vehicles not used as a residence must be valued at $4,500 or less to be eligible for
aid. The property limit for a mobile home used as a residence is $15,000. Only one
motor vehicle may be retained per household.

* Cash on hand or in a bank account is valued at $100 or less for single applicants,
$200 or less for couple/family applicants, or $1,500 or less after GR is approved.

+ Real Property (residence) has an assessed value of $34,000 or less and applicants
agree to sign a lien, allowing the County to recover GR payments received under
certain circumstances.

An individual is ineligible for GR if they are:

+ In violation of probation or parole.
+ Fleeing to avoid prosecution or custody/confinement after a felony conviction.

GR APPLICATION

Residents of Los Angeles County may apply for GR in person in a Department of Public
Social Services GR district office, over the phone by calling the Customer Service Center
at (866) 613-3777, by mail, fax, or online through BenefitsCal.

SUBSTANCE USE DISORDER REQUIREMENT

GR applicants may be pre-screened for a Substance Use Disorder (SUD) if there is a
reasonable suspicion of a disorder. If there is an indication of a disorder from the
pre-screening, the GR applicant is referred to the Department of Public Health for a formal
screening. If at the screening appointment, the applicant is determined to have a SUD,
the applicant may still be approved for GR if all other eligibility criteria are met, and must
participate in a treatment program as a condition for continued eligibility for GR.
